etymologies.heading: Etymology 1
paragraphs: From Middle English caggen (“to tie, fasten, bind”), probably from Old Norse. Compare Old Norse kǫgurr (“quilt”), kǫgurbarn (“swaddled child”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology 2
senses: (falconry) A circular frame on which cadgers carry hawks for sale.
To carry hawks and other birds of prey.
(UK, Scotland, dialect) To carry, as a burden.
